text:
Sara: Heads-up: nightly perf CI shows p99 token latency +18% on the serving runtime after last merge. Rolling window spike visible around 03:10 UTC. tagging #eng-runtime 
Kai: saw the alert. dashboard: https://observability.redwood/services/serving/p99?range=24h 
Sara: Suspect area: batching heuristics change from PR #5421 (dynamic batch window tweak). Can someone try to repro locally with KV-heavy load? 
Miguel: I can try on my workstation. Which harness do you want me to run? 
Sara: use ./tools/perf_runner --profile=kv_workload --seq-len=256 --clients=32 --duration=600. Enable kernel trace too if possible. 
ci-bot: nightly-build 1978123300 completed. perf-regression rule fired: serving/p99 increased by 18% vs baseline. 
Kai: also set ENV KERNEL_TRACE=1 and KV_CACHE=true to mirror prod. 
Miguel: starting run now. will post flamegraphs and a short diff. 
Miguel: repro locally. p99 up ~22% compared to v1.14.0. Reverted the batch-window tweak locally and p99 drops back to baseline. 
Adrian: interesting. can you capture the trace and grep for batch window flush events? maybe the heuristic is causing more small batches. 
Miguel: attaching snippet of the hot path and sample log (reduced):
```
[2026-03-18T03:02:11Z] batcher: seq=256 window_ms=3 flush_count=412
[2026-03-18T03:02:11Z] batcher: seq=256 window_ms=1 flush_count=1123
[2026-03-18T03:02:11Z] kvcache: hit_rate=0.78 evictions=3
```
Miguel: looks like window_ms reduced from 3->1 in the new heuristic causing many small flushes under KV pressure. 
Sara: ok plan: git-bisect between v1.14.0 and main, but run an automated perf check. we'll use the perf_bisect harness. Steps: 
```
git bisect start v1.14.0 main
export WARM_SECS=30 KERNEL_TRACE=1 KV_CACHE=1
git bisect run ./tools/perf_bisect.sh --target p99 --profile kv_workload --seq-len 256
```
Kai: perf_bisect.sh needs to warm caches and run 3 iterations per commit. I'll start a bisect job on a canary node. 
Miguel: FYI I ran a quick manual bisection and pinned commit 9c4b3f8 as the first bad commit (the batch-window tweak). 
Adrian: if that's the commit, what's the minimal change? Could we hotpatch a guard that keeps the previous window when kv cache pressure > 0.8? 
Kai: preparing a revert PR now for the merge commit. If bisect confirms 9c4b3f8, I'll open PR 5470: revert "batch-window tweak" and tag it hotfix. 
Sara: we should prefer a feature-flag rollback if possible, but revert is fine for immediate mitigation. Also add a perf regression test to CI for seq-len=256 kv profile. 
devops-bot: deploy canary will be created once PR 5470 is merged to canary. 
Miguel: canary run with revert applied shows p99 back to baseline in my local sim. 
Kai: merged revert to canary at 1978124000 and started rollout. monitoring for 20m. 
Sara: monitor dashboards and traces. if canary stable, promote to prod. Also record the bisect run and attach commit id in the incident. 
Kai: canary smoke passed at 1978124750, metrics stable for 25m. promoting to prod now. 
devops-bot: prod deploy started at 1978125400 by Kai. status: in-progress. 
Adrian: follow-up: I'll submit a defensive change that reintroduces the heuristic but gated behind a KV pressure check and add unit perf tests. Miguel can help with microbenchmarks. 
Miguel: opening PR for a guarded heuristic + CI perf test. link will be in the incident ticket. 
Sara: excellent. incident ticket created: INC-2026-0318-serve-perf. add links to the bisect logs and perf artifacts. 
Kai: note for postmortem: add synthetic KV workload to nightly perf suite so this doesn't regress unnoticed. 
Sara: thanks everyone for quick turnaround :thumbsup: 
Miguel: will also add a small benchmark that runs in CI against a dockerized runtime to catch kernel selection changes. 
Sara: closing loop once the PRs are merged and the CI test lands.
